content:
I've always been confused by the spelling of the whatsnew in command. There are two issues here:

  • The space between whats and new is not reflected in the name. Compare with e.g. to_additive.
  • The command is not meant to end up in the final code, so it should start with #. Compare e.g. #guard_msgs in or #count_hearbeats in

Do people agree it should be spelled as #whats_new in?
Can we keep whatsnew as a deprecation for muscle memory?
Or perhaps whatever the attribute is that suggests corrections when you make a typo
Yes of course we would add a syntax deprecation, rather than removing it altogether. So the old spelling would still work, but also omit a warning

Alternatively, we could have whats new in, similar to the existing deprecate to.
Or would deprecate to get the same treatment?
#whats_new still fails to capture the apostrophe in "what's". Personally I would rather something like #env_diff.
There is some precedent for removing the apostrophe, in to_additive (dont_translate := ...).
